look_here_first: FOLLOW THE SMALL HAIRY SHOOT TO ITS FLOWERING HEADS. E. ophthalmica (Florida hammock sandmat) typically makes a LOW PROSTRATE hairy colony with small opposite, slightly unequal, finely toothed leaves. At the END of each main shoot or SHORT LEAFY side shoot, many tiny cyathia crowd into a round HEAD (glomerule). E. hirta also has terminal heads but additionally makes AXILLARY heads, often on extended LEAFLESS stalks: seeing just one terminal head does not prove ophthalmica. E. hypericifolia also forms dense heads but generally has SMOOTH STEMS and smooth capsules; E. nutans makes looser leafy clusters and larger leaves. FNA describes ophthalmica's minute capsule as finely APPRESSED-HAIRY, its stipules as narrow and sometimes divided, and its four-angled seeds with a few FAINT CROSSWISE wrinkles. Our existing images SUPPORT head placement, leaf/stem hairs and mat habit, but NOT clear capsule hairs, tiny stipules or seed sculpture. No Hays County native-range finding should be inferred from these mostly nonlocal source photos.
photo_note: SEVEN real source photographs installed, including five photographed panels with 17 actual pixel-reviewed arrows; two new macro photographs by Lucy Cash and karlabalrey show terminal head placement, thin hairs on STEM and LEAF, but NOT diagnostic tiny capsule hairs, true stipules or mature seeds. synonyms: Euphorbia hirta var. ophthalmica (Pers.) Allem & Irgang
taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia ophthalmica Pers. (POWO/WCVP; Flora of North America). Formerly combined with or treated as variety of E. hirta; diagnostic terminal-only small heads, prostrate habit and small leaves separate these concepts.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. Opposite leaves, milky latex, cyathia (tiny reproductive structures), 3-lobed dry fruit.
morphology_keys.habit: Usually prostrate, rarely ascending, annual (occasionally short-lived perennial) from taproot; slender shoots 6–22 cm. A low spreading habit is suggestive, never sufficient alone.
morphology_keys.stems: Fine short appressed hairs (strigillose) mixed with longer spreading hairs (hirsute), often both on the same plant.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; ovate to oblong, 4–13 × 3–7 mm, asymmetric base, coarse fine teeth (coarsely serrulate), usually with 3 veins emerging near base; center may carry red blotch but many leaves do not.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, narrow subulate-filiform scales, entire or divided into 2–4 slender triangular/threadlike segments, 0.9–1.5 mm, hairy; lacking dark round glands at base. A magnified true node is needed to distinguish from ordinary hairs.
morphology_keys.flowering_cluster: Dense CAPITATE terminal glomerules; at ends of main stems or very short leafy side shoots. Small reduced bractlike leaves occur beneath them. Unlike E. hirta, not separate axillary flower heads on long leafless stalks.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Tiny involucres about 0.5–0.7 × 0.4–0.6 mm with fine hairs; four yellow-green to pinkish glands, with thin white/pink rims or very small appendages, sometimes without obvious appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Ovoid three-lobed capsule 1–1.2 × 1–1.3 mm, strigillose (finely appressed-hairy), not smooth/glabrous.
morphology_keys.seed: Orange-brown to pinkish, narrowly ovoid, sharply four-angled; 0.7–0.9(–1.1) × about 0.5 mm; usually shallow wrinkling and 3–6 faint transverse ridges, occasionally smooth-looking.
best_field_traits: prostrate hairy stems terminating in dense round cyathium heads

small opposite asymmetric 4–13 mm leaves with coarsely serrulate margins

narrow sometimes divided stipules at nodes
mature 4-angled 0.7–0.9 mm seeds with low transverse wrinkles

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compare actual HEAD PLACEMENT first: ophthalmica's crowded heads at shoot tips and short LEAFY branches; hirta has terminal as well as AXILLARY heads often on leafless stalks. Do not identify ophthalmica solely from a terminal head. Hypericifolia may have equally compact head clusters but is generally glabrous, nutans has larger leaves and looser flowering groups. Microscopic differences in fruit hair, stipules and seed sculpture still need new licensed macro photographs.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: TRACE THE HEAD TO ITS STEM — THEN LOOK FOR FRUIT AND SEEDS
steps: Find short often reddish hairy shoots pressed near the soil; show a complete branch from the leaf node to the compact round flower head.

Count the FLOWER-HEAD POSITIONS: ophthalmica grows dense heads at the ends of main and SHORT LEAFY side branches; E. hirta may additionally carry axillary clusters on LONG LEAFLESS stalks. A single terminal head never settles the pair.
At 10× look for mixed short appressed and longer spreading stem hairs; several existing photos show visible LEAF hairs, not provable mature capsule hairs.
Photograph both small opposite leaves with finely toothed margins and slightly UNEQUAL bases; a red center blotch alone says little.
To separate species with confidence, isolate a TRUE mature ovoid 3-lobed fruit and photograph fine appressed hairs on the CAPSULE (not just hairy leaf or cyathial involucre).
At 20–30× check real 0.9–1.5 mm slender/divided stipules at the leaf bases and a true detached 0.7–0.9 mm four-angled seed with 3–6 faint crosswise wrinkles; include mm scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Microscopic CAPSULE hairs, genuine nodal stipule forms and seed ridges are still based on Flora of North America text only, not on the currently verified photographed structures. Texas naturalized versus native status is NOT evaluated; FNA does not include Texas among the states it documents for this species.

visual_comparison.overlay_note: A true leafy shoot ending in a compact head is informative but NOT alone enough to exclude E. hirta, which can also show terminal heads. The key is whether additional long leafless-stalk axillary heads occur. Hair on the leaf is not evidence of hair on the mature capsule. Published images do not establish native status in Hays County.
